chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you lend dirhams, and then they bring you back something better than them, there is no harm in that, provided there was no condition (of specific repayment) between you."
ai.seo_question: Can a lender accept better quality coins when repaying a loan of the same currency type without prior agreement?
ai.summary: In the context of classical Shia fiqh, this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *qard* (interest-free loan) and *riba* (usury) by permitting the acceptance of superior quality coins as repayment, provided no prior condition (*shart*) was made to return the exact same coins. This ruling highlights the scholarly emphasis on the lender's intent and the absence of a fixed exchange condition, distinguishing it from commercial sales where quality differences might imply hidden interest. It reflects the practical legal flexibility in early Islamic economic transactions regarding currency valuation.
